aarti.tek: Om, victory to you, Citragupta, O Lord; Master, victory to you, Citragupta, O Lord. You bring to fulfilment the fruit your devotees wish for.
aarti.pad1: You destroy obstacles, bring good fortune and give joy to the saints. You protect your devotees; your glory has spread over the three worlds. ॥1॥
aarti.pad2: Your form is four-armed, your image dark, and a yellow silk robe shines upon you. Mother Irāvatī and Dakṣiṇā adorn your left side. ॥2॥
aarti.pad3: You remove suffering and destroy the wicked; you are the Lord who dwells within all. Destroyer of creation, remover of people's sorrow, you appeared, Master. ॥3॥
aarti.pad4: Pen, inkpot, conch and record look most splendid in your hand. The vaijayantī garland of forest flowers charms the hearts of the three worlds. ॥4॥
aarti.pad5: You took up the office of the throne, and Brahmā rejoiced. The thirty-three crore gods hastened to your feet. ॥5॥
aarti.pad6: King Saudāsa and Bhīṣma the grandsire remembered you; swiftly, without delay, you gave them the fruit they wished for. ॥6॥
aarti.pad7: Wife, son and sister all act for their own well-being. Where shall I go, whose refuge shall I seek? Leaving you, O sustainer, where could I go? ॥7॥
aarti.pad8: You are my brother, my father and my master; whose refuge should I take? Without you there is no other in whom I could place my hope. ॥8॥
aarti.pad9: Those who sing the āratī of Citragupta with love are surely freed from the round of the eighty-four lakh births and gain the fruit they wish for. ॥9॥
aarti.pad10: You are the judge who dwells in Vaikuṇṭha, and you write down sin and merit. We are in your refuge; we hope in no other. ॥10॥
